findings.title: The named threshold before full disclosure
findings.claim: Within the host-surah sequence, the name in the basmala functions as an entry handle for al-Qari'ah, which is introduced by a repeated designation before its nature is unfolded.
findings.mechanism: The focus carrier بِسْمِ holds the accepted name-and-designation facet. The host repeats ٱلْقَارِعَةُ in 101:1, 101:2, and 101:3, while أَدْرَىٰكَ in 101:3 turns that designation into a question of coming to know; the naming function therefore meets a staged disclosure of the named event.
findings.reader_payoff: The opening name becomes a concrete threshold: the reader receives a handle for the coming event before the text discloses what that event does.
findings.containment: The ordinary reading remains 'in the name of Allah'. This does not claim that the basmala names al-Qari'ah, reveal its full meaning in advance, or state a thesis for the surah.

epistemic.reason: The accepted name branch has a direct focus carrier, and the supplied host sequence visibly repeats a designation before asking what it is; the threshold function is a bounded contextual inference from that contact.

branch_activations.branch_gloss: ad, adlandırma ve ad ya da nitelik bakımından denklik
branch_activations.facet_statement: Ad, bir varlığı tanıtan ve ondan söz etmeyi sağlayan söz veya anlamdır.
branch_activations.carrier: The focus form بِسْمِ carries the name/designation function in the construct بِسْمِ اللَّهِ.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The host uses the definite designation ٱلْقَارِعَةُ repeatedly and places it inside the question 'what is al-Qari'ah?' while asking how it can be known.
branch_activations.activation: The focus name function meets the host's named-but-not-yet-unfolded event, making naming the first grasp by which the coming disclosure can be entered.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The basmala's name is perceptible as a threshold that gives the host event a speakable designation before the event's force is described.
branch_activations.boundary: This is a local host-context effect; it does not turn the basmala into a title for the surah or claim that the name itself explains al-Qari'ah.

findings.title: Mercy at the edge of heat
findings.claim: Against the host's closing image of a hot fire, the two mercy epithets in the basmala can be heard as active esirgeme and iyilik at the edge of danger, while the fire remains fully present.
findings.mechanism: The focus carriers الرَّحْمَٰنِ and الرَّحِيمِ hold the mercy branch's active result of protecting and doing good. The host ends with نَارٌ حَامِيَةٌ, an independent image of consuming heat; that threat gives the protective consequence of mercy a concrete local situation.
findings.reader_payoff: The mercy words become a live protective relation around the host's final heat rather than two detached descriptive titles.
findings.containment: The plain basmala remains an invocation in Allah's merciful name. This does not cancel the host's judgement or fire, promise rescue, or equate fire with mercy.

epistemic.reason: The branch source explicitly joins mercy to active esirgeme and iyilik, while the host supplies the concrete danger; the protective framing is a contextual inference rather than a stated equivalence.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Bu iç yöneliş, acınan kişiyi esirgemeyi ve ona iyilikte bulunmayı gerektiren etkin bir sonuç taşır.
branch_activations.carrier: The paired mercy epithets carry mercy as an orientation that reaches the other through esirgeme and iyilik.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The host closes with نَارٌ حَامِيَةٌ, explicitly placing the human outcome beside fire and intense heat.
branch_activations.activation: The danger named by the host supplies the exposed recipient and concrete circumstance in which mercy's active protecting and doing-good consequence becomes perceptible.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: At the host boundary, Allah's mercy is heard as a protective action held in view beside the final heat, not merely as an unlocated quality.
branch_activations.boundary: The relation remains contextual and contained; it does not state a theological guarantee that the fire is withdrawn or that every outcome is protected.

findings.title: Mercy given a relational contour
findings.claim: The host's word for 'his mother' gives the mercy names a bounded relational contour: mercy can be sensed here as nearness and a bond, set beside the host's image of a return that is an abyss.
findings.mechanism: The focus carriers الرَّحْمَٰنِ and الرَّحِيمِ can contact the accepted close-kinship facet through the independent relation named by أُمُّهُ in 101:9. The following هَاوِيَةٌ makes that relation matter by placing the person's point of return under a severe image.
findings.reader_payoff: The paired mercy titles gain the shape of a relation that stands close to a person at the very point where the host describes a terrifying return.
findings.containment: The basmala still names Allah as merciful. This does not make Allah a biological relative, translate mercy as 'mother', or decide what أُمُّهُ means beyond the supplied host wording.

epistemic.reason: The host directly supplies a maternal relation and the branch directly supplies close kinship, but their contact with the mercy epithets is an explicitly bounded contextual inference.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Ortak soydan gelme, kişiler arasında yakın ve kalıcı bir soy ilişkisi kurar.
branch_activations.carrier: The mercy epithets carry a relation of nearness in addition to their ordinary mercy description when the supplied context gives that relation a concrete human form.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The host names أُمُّهُ, 'his mother', as a direct familial relation.
branch_activations.activation: The maternal relation gives the focus mercy field a relational shape, and هَاوِيَةٌ makes the loss of a secure return the local pressure against which that nearness is heard.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The basmala's mercy becomes locally perceptible as closeness to the vulnerable person, alongside the host's abyss image.
branch_activations.boundary: The activation concerns a contextual relational contour only; it does not assert shared biological origin, maternal theology, or a replacement for the ordinary divine epithet.

findings.title: Mercy as an enclosing interior
findings.claim: The maternal and abyss images in 101:9 let the mercy names carry a second, more spatial contour: an enclosing interior that is perceptible at the brink of falling.
findings.mechanism: The focus carriers الرَّحْمَٰنِ and الرَّحِيمِ contact the accepted womb facet through أُمُّهُ and its associated maternal source, while هَاوِيَةٌ supplies the contrasting image of descent into an open depth. The contact turns the womb facet into a bounded holding image without making it the literal gloss of the focus words.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can feel why the mercy formula matters at the threshold of the host's abyss: it supplies an image of being held before the text presents falling and heat.
findings.containment: The ordinary mercy reading remains intact. This is not an anatomical claim about Allah, not a claim that 'mother' means 'womb' in the host, and not a promise that the abyss is removed.

epistemic.reason: The branch is an accepted womb sense and the host supplies a maternal word plus a descent image, but the enclosing-space reading is a multi-step contextual inference and is kept explicitly qualified.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Dişi bedenindeki bu iç organ, yavrunun oluşup geliştiği yer ve onu karın içinde taşıyan kap işlevindedir.
branch_activations.carrier: The mercy epithets carry a possible holding-and-protection image when their focus context meets the supplied maternal and enclosing-space cues.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The host gives أُمُّهُ, a maternal source, immediately alongside هَاوِيَةٌ, an abyss or falling place.
branch_activations.activation: The maternal source activates the womb's carrying interior, while the abyss supplies the threatened loss of containment; together they make the mercy formula locally legible as an enclosing contrast at the brink of descent.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The opening mercy can be sensed as a holding interior that stands beside, and therefore sharpens, the host's image of falling into an abyss.
branch_activations.boundary: Only the spatial image is retained; the branch is not applied as a literal bodily attribute or used to settle the host's doctrinal image of the afterlife.

findings.title: Mercy extended across the worlds
findings.claim: The explicit Fātiḥa overlay in 1:2 adds a scope delta: the mercy named in the basmala is heard as reaching the worlds that are placed under Allah's sustaining lordship.
findings.mechanism: The focus mercy carriers contact the branch's divine-use facet, where mercy's breadth reaches created beings. In 1:2, رَبِّ supplies the sustaining relation and ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ supplies its full field; this is a local scope-setting contact rather than a repetition of the focus words.
findings.reader_payoff: The two mercy epithets gain a concrete horizon: their reach is heard against the supplied phrase naming the worlds under Allah's care.
findings.containment: The primary basmala remains an invocation in Allah's merciful name. This overlay does not import a whole-surah thesis, claim an exhaustive doctrine of divine mercy, or treat the repeated mercy phrase in 1:3 as a new trigger.

epistemic.reason: The supplied divine-use facet explicitly concerns mercy reaching created beings, and the external ayah directly supplies the sustaining relation and its world-wide object; the overlay is specific to the focus mercy words.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Tanrı hakkında kullanıldığında esirgemenin genişliği ve yaratılmışlara iyilik olarak ulaşması belirginleşir.
branch_activations.carrier: The paired focus epithets carry divine mercy whose effect can reach created beings.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The external overlay calls Allah رَبِّ, the sustaining lord, of ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ, the worlds.
branch_activations.activation: The external sustaining relation and its world-wide object give the focus mercy branch a specific field of reach, so the epithets are heard as extending through the named worlds.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: In the overlay, the basmala's mercy is perceptible as broad care extending across the worlds named in 1:2.
branch_activations.boundary: This is limited to the supplied 1:2 overlay and the branch's divine breadth; it does not generalize beyond the packet or make the external ayah a replacement for the basmala.

findings.title: The named one as the worshipped one
findings.claim: The explicit Fātiḥa overlay in 1:5 adds the worship relation that makes the basmala's divine name concrete: Allah is heard as the one to whom the worship act is directed.
findings.mechanism: The focus carrier اللَّهِ contacts the accepted branch's worshipped-being facet. The external verb نَعْبُدُ supplies an independent act of worship, while 1:2 supplies the same divine name in the overlay's preceding address; the contact moves the name from designation alone into the relation of worship.
findings.reader_payoff: The name in the opening formula acquires an immediate relational answer: the one named is also the one before whom the worshipping 'we' stands.
findings.containment: The basmala's proper-name reading remains. This does not turn every use of Allah into a worship statement, collapse the Fātiḥa into the basmala, or claim more than the supplied worship relation.

epistemic.reason: The accepted branch directly includes the worshipped-being facet and the external text supplies the worship act, but the referent relation is assembled across the supplied overlay rather than stated in one focus phrase.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Eylemden türeyen varlık anlamı, kendisine tapınılan varlığı veya tapınma konusu sayılan nesneyi gösterir.
branch_activations.carrier: The focus proper name اللَّهِ identifies the divine referent of the opening formula.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The external ayah states نَعْبُدُ, 'we worship', in a direct second-person address, with 1:2 naming Allah in the same supplied overlay.
branch_activations.activation: The worship act meets the named divine referent and activates the branch's derived sense of the one who is worshipped.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The basmala's Allah is locally heard not only as the name invoked but as the one toward whom the supplied worship act is directed.
branch_activations.boundary: The finding depends on the explicit overlay relation between 1:2 and 1:5; it does not add an unprovided grammatical identity or extend the worship facet to unrelated context.

findings.title: Mercy heard as received favor
findings.claim: The explicit Fātiḥa overlay in 1:7 adds an enacted form of mercy: the basmala's mercy names can be heard in relation to the favor bestowed upon those who receive it.
findings.mechanism: The focus carriers الرَّحْمَٰنِ and الرَّحِيمِ contact the mercy branch's active result of doing good. The independent verb أَنْعَمْتَ in 1:7 describes favor reaching named people, turning the focus attribute into a relation between beneficent action and its recipients.
findings.reader_payoff: Mercy acquires a visible movement from giver to recipient, so the paired titles can be heard as an action that arrives in a person's condition.
findings.containment: The ordinary divine mercy reading remains. This does not identify the favored people beyond the supplied text, rank them against the angered or straying, or import a complete Fātiḥa interpretation.

epistemic.reason: The accepted mercy branch explicitly includes active iyilik, and the external ayah supplies a direct favor action with recipients; the resulting giver-to-recipient relation is a specific focus contact.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Bu iç yöneliş, acınan kişiyi esirgemeyi ve ona iyilikte bulunmayı gerektiren etkin bir sonuç taşır.
branch_activations.carrier: The paired mercy epithets carry the active good that mercy brings to another.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The external ayah uses أَنْعَمْتَ, 'you bestowed favor', and explicitly attaches that action to people.
branch_activations.activation: The bestowed-favor action supplies a concrete recipient-facing form for the mercy branch's active good, so the focus names are heard through an arrival of beneficence.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The basmala's mercy is locally perceptible as favor that can reach people, not only as a quality attributed to its source.
branch_activations.boundary: The overlay retains the supplied favor relation only; it does not identify a complete class of favored people or adjudicate the paired exclusions in 1:7.
